messages:
Priya: Heads up — I’m seeing a spike in reconnects from EU edge right after the console sampling rollout. Console shows a lot of 'probe' events but no route-swap logs. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/edge-reconnects :eyes:
Alex: Saw that too. Sampling rate bumped to 50% for the EU probe experiment (.1 -> .5) and client-side jitter looks synchronized. Lots of concurrent probes land on the same proxy pool -> thundering reconnects.
Theo: Could this be the sticky-route fallback we flipped yesterday? If quota-check returns a 204 empty-chunk, some clients treat that as EOF and reconnect immediately.
Jess: Yup — our fetch loop treats a 204 with no body as termination. Short-term options: change client to treat 204 as keepalive OR change proxy to send a small single newline for keepalive responses.
Alex: Also noticed telemetry gap: the probe sampler strips X-Event-Id in the proxy layer so console dedupe thinks those are separate events; counts don't match actual reconnects.
Priya: Proposed plan: 1) roll sampler back to .1 for EU, 2) patch client to ignore 204-as-eof in 2.3.0, 3) proxy hotfix to emit "
" keepalive for 204s as a low-risk fallback, 4) add a console flag to split probe vs route-swap metrics. Thoughts? :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy: proxy-hotfix/v1.2.3 started rollout to eu-edge-canary — CI passed, canaries 1/3 healthy so far.
Theo: I’ll pick up the client patch. Will open a PR, add unit for 204 handling, and coordinate canary.
Jess: I can own the console flag and telemetry mapping fix. I’ll add an annotation to backfill counts for the last 6 hours.
Priya: Thanks — once infra confirms canary looks stable, we can slowly increase sampling or run the experiment with staggered jitter. Also add a short note in the rollout playbook about 204 semantics.
Alex: One small follow-up: add a probe header (X-Probe-Sampler: <id>) so we can filter these events in traces. That should help dedupe without changing upstream ids.
Theo: +1. Will include header in the client PR so end-to-end traces line up.
Priya: Great. Keeping this thread for coordination — please post PR links and canary results here.
